name: contextforge-v2
description: Desktop app that lets one developer use many AIs to build games without losing context or breaking dependencies.
//: tree-sitter-typescript@0.23.2 and tree-sitter-gdscript@6.1.0 still declare peer deps on tree-sitter ^0.21.x, so installing alongside tree-sitter 0.25 needs --legacy-peer-deps. See D17.

scripts.postinstall: echo "If npm failed on a peer-dependency conflict: use 'npm install --legacy-peer-deps' (see D17)."
scripts.dist:appimage: npm run typecheck && npm run build:ui -w @contextforge/app && electron-builder --linux AppImage
scripts.verify: npm run check:boundaries && npm run check:three && npm run typecheck && npm run check:svelte && npm run lint:prefabs && npm test

//build: electron-builder config. Five decisions here were forced by this being an npm workspace, and each is commented where it applies: (1) `directories.app: packages/app` selects electron-builder's two-package-json layout, so the app's OWN package.json declares the runtime dependencies and node_modules is collected from there rather than from the root, which has none. (2) `extraMetadata.main` points at the real entry, `dist/electron/main.js` relative to packages/app. There is no `main` key in electron-builder's schema (verified against app-builder-lib/scheme.json), so this cannot be set the obvious way. (3) `files` opens with `!**/*` to make the rest an allowlist, because in a workspace the bare `node_modules` electron-builder would pick up by default is only the root's, so every package must be listed — including `node-gyp-build`, which is a RUNTIME dependency of all four tree-sitter packages (`require('node-gyp-build')` in their index.js) and not a build-time one; a package without it starts, then dies on the first parse. (4) It lists `dist/ipc.js` and `dist/errors.js` as well as `dist/electron/**`, because `tsc` emits `src/ipc.ts` to `dist/ipc.js` (NOT into `dist/electron/`) and `dist/electron/ipcHandlers.js` imports `../ipc.js` — a package built without those two files starts, then dies with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. (5) It lists `esbuild` and its `@esbuild/linux-x64` binary, because `dist/electron/prefabLoader.js` does a top-level `import { build } from 'esbuild'` — esbuild is a RUNTIME dependency of the main process, not a build-time one, so a package without it throws an uncaught ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND in the main process the moment a project is opened. That one is a devDependency in packages/app/package.json ONLY because of this allowlist mistake; it is declared in `dependencies` now. `asarUnpack` keeps the tree-sitter binaries as real files, because a native addon cannot be dlopen'd from inside an asar. See notes/lane-packaging.md and docs/RUNNING.md.

linux.synopsis: AI context manager for game projects
linux.description: Reads a game project off disk, extracts a dependency graph from the real source files, and compiles that graph into an AI-ready prompt. Runs entirely locally.

entry.Name: ContextForge
entry.Comment: Compile a game project into AI-ready context, preview patches, and edit scenes
